collection.description: An elder's hut is so full of things that it is time for a change: give some away, or tidy and keep everything.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s hut is full. Baskets inside baskets. Shells on every shelf. Seven digging sticks, three of them broken. A wooden fish (subject.he/she) carved fifty years ago. Today (subject) trips over a pile of old nets for the third time and decides that something has to change.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (subject) puts a few things outside the door: a good basket, a nice shell, a carved bowl. By evening they're all gone to people who seem pleased with them. (subject.He/She) sees (child), a child, walking past with the bowl, filled with berries. (subject) feels lighter, somehow. The wooden fish, of course, stays. Some things aren't going anywhere.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) spends the whole day sorting. (subject.He/She) finds things (subject.he/she) forgot (subject.he/she) owned. (subject.He/She) finds a toy (subject.he/she) made for a child who is now a grandparent (subject.him/her)self. In the end (subject.he/she) throws away exactly one broken digging stick, stacks everything else more neatly, and decides (subject.he/she) likes (subject.his/her) full, crowded, crammed hut very much, thank you.
